justification_chain: (at b2 c11) <- (push c13 c12 c11 b2 left), which needs at-player c13, at b2 c12, clear c11
(at-player c13) <- (move c12 c13 right), which needs at-player c12 and clear c13
(at-player c12) <- (push c11 c12 c13 b2 right), which needs at-player c11, at b2 c12, clear c13

so one push does all the cheating at once: it adds at-player c12 while its deletes of `at b2 c12` and `clear c13` are dropped, and the player then walks into the dead-end c13 and pushes the box the other way

structural_signature.proved_for: width-1 `no_deleting_action` theorems on this sokoban encoding (which is what all three of rnd0021's theorems are)
structural_signature.step_1: A pattern {at(b,c)} with n_deleting_actions = 0 means grounding left no push instance with (?b=b, ?from=c) at all. In the delete relaxation from a state containing at(b,c), no atom at(b,c') with c' != c can ever be added, because every push that adds one needs some at(b,y) that is not there and can only itself come from a push of b.
structural_signature.step_2: Therefore, if the goal requires at(b,g) with g != c, the relaxation is dead too. A theorem can escape the relaxation ONLY IF c = g, i.e. the pattern atom IS a goal atom -- a box frozen on its own goal.
structural_signature.step_3: But `excludes_goal` then has to find a mutex between at(b,g) and some goal atom, and it cannot be at(b,g) itself (that atom is h^2-possible, it holds in a reachable state). So the mutex must be with a DIFFERENT goal atom -- which means h^2 has proved the goal conjunction inconsistent, i.e. h^2 has proved the whole instance unsolvable.
structural_signature.conclusion: The real gap is h^2 vs h^1. The carver proves goal-exclusion with an h^2 pairwise-reachability fixpoint (deadlock_carver/mutex.py); Fast Downward's translator settles a task before search with h^1 delete-relaxation reachability. A carver theorem beats the translator exactly on instances h^2 proves unsolvable but h^1 does not -- and there it beats it only through the one theorem whose pattern is a goal atom.

rnd0021_confirms_it.but_h1_does_not: FD's translator built a 373-fact task and blind had to expand all 92 states
rnd0021_confirms_it.only_theorem_whose_pattern_is_a_goal_ato: at(b1,c41) -- and it is the only one with witnesses (11); the other two have 0

structural_signature.geometry_that_makes_h1_fail_here: a dead-end cell d (c13) whose only free neighbour is the box's cell f (c12), with the box's goal g (c11) on the opposite side of f. Truly: pushing f->g needs the player on d, and the player can only reach d through f, which the box occupies. Relaxed: the push f->d puts the player on f while the box stays on f and d stays clear, so the player walks f->d and pushes f->g.

can_it_arise_in_far_N.answer: no, and not by luck -- it is impossible
can_it_arise_in_far_N.reason_1: far{N} is solvable, so h^2 cannot prove its goal conjunction inconsistent, so by step_3 no theorem can have a goal atom as its pattern; every far{N} theorem is at(b, non-goal frozen corner), and by step_2 every such theorem is inside the relaxation. n_theorem_dead_outside_relaxation = 0 on far{N} is therefore a THEOREM about that family, not a measurement.
can_it_arise_in_far_N.reason_2: far{N} is an open N x N room with no interior walls, so it has no degree-1 free cell for the relaxation's dead-end cheat to exploit, and its goals are edge cells rather than the frozen corners.
can_it_arise_in_far_N.implication: the audit's section 3 table could never have found this, at any size.

structural_signature.empirical_check: attacks/verify/sweep_soundness.json -- 42 instances of the a3 family analysed; rnd0021 is the ONLY one with witnesses. door-swap is also h^2-unsolvable with a live relaxation on 47 states, but none of its 11 theorem patterns is a goal atom, so it has 0 witnesses -- exactly what step_2/step_3 predict.

honest_caveats: rnd0021 is unsolvable from its initial state. The 11 witnesses are reachable, genuinely dead, and missed by FD's relaxation, so the counterexample is real -- but it is not the 'interaction deadlock inside a solvable instance' case section 4 hoped for. Here the theorem is a whole-instance unsolvability certificate wearing a deadlock's clothes.
Because every state of rnd0021 is truly dead, this instance can never test carver soundness. That was checked elsewhere (42-instance sweep plus the audit's own far4/5/6 rows).

All three theorems are width-1 `no_deleting_action`. The structural argument above is proved for that class only; a width-2 `deleting_actions_blocked` theorem could in principle escape the relaxation by another route, and nothing here rules that out or in.
One domain, one encoding, one planner -- the same caveats DEADLOCK_CLAIM.md section 6 already carries.
